properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by the dev_storyflow fleet, 2026-09-02, and it is the sharpest thing in that report.

THEIR CASE, in their words: they wrote a capability whose description said in capitals *"THE DROPLET STILL RUNS THE OLD SCRIPT ... tonight's cron will capture the wrong volume again."* Twenty minutes later they installed the fix and called `set_capability_status(realized)`. **The description still said the droplet ran the old script.** Status said delivered; prose said not started; same node; nothing flagged it. They caught it only by re-reading their own text.

⭐ **THEY ALSO NAMED WHY VIGILANCE IS NOT THE ANSWER**, and the detail is what makes this worth recording: their own design already holds an entire epoch about state-describing text rotting (`epoch:2026_08_17_state_documents_rot_silently`), and the person who rotted a node inside twenty minutes had READ that epoch the same day. In their words: *"Vigilance is not the countermeasure; something mechanical has to be."*

**REFLOW2 HAS HIT THIS ON ITS OWN GRAPH.** `chg:content-store-built` is titled "cap:content-store built — realized, checked, **and its description no longer says PLANNED**". Somebody had to notice and fix the prose by hand. So this is not a consumer-only problem.

THEIR PROPOSED FIX IS UNUSUALLY CHEAP AND IS EXPLICITLY *NOT* A DETECTOR: *"when `set_capability_status` / `set_verification_status` / `set_epoch_status` moves a node forward, the tool already knows the description was not touched in that call. It could say so — 'status is now `realized`; `description` was last written when status was `in_progress` — does it still read true?' ... It does not need to be a detector, a gap, or a nudge; it needs to be one sentence in a return value."*

OPTIONS TURNED OVER, none preferred:

· **A — One sentence in the `set_*_status` reply**, exactly as they propose. Costs nothing, fires at the moment of the change, and asks rather than asserts. ⚠️ It is a NUDGE AT A MOMENT, so it reaches only the agent making that call. A description that rots because the WORLD changed, with no status move at all, is untouched.

· **B — Track when the prose was last written.** The reply can only say "not touched in this call"; saying "last written when status was X" needs a stored timestamp or a snapshot lookup. Richer, and it is the version that would still be true a week later. ⚠️ New per-node bookkeeping for a sentence.

· **C — A detector: status and description disagree.** The other entry in the same file proposes the sibling — sweeping `planned` capabilities for descriptions asserting they are built, which found six. ⚠️ **AND THE REPORTER DISPROVED THEIR OWN VERSION WHILE PROPOSING IT**: their first regex returned ten hits, four of which were NEGATIONS ("STATUS is planned: nothing is built") matched on the word "built". They wrote: *"the detector I wrote to find dishonest nodes was itself 40% wrong on first run."* A textual contradiction detector is an LLM judgement, not a grep, and this project's doctrine is that a detector reports and never judges.

· **D — Do nothing mechanical; put it in the skills.** `revise-design` is where an agent stands when it has just changed a status. ⚠️ The measured counter is brutal: the person who rotted the node had read the epoch about exactly this, the same day.

⚠️ THE HONEST TENSION, which is theirs and worth keeping: *"the tool is careful about DESTROYING prose and silent about prose that has quietly become FALSE. The second is the more common loss."* The `revision`/`replaced` block they praise twice in the same report is proof reflow2 CAN be careful at exactly the right moment — it just guards the wrong hazard.
properties.name: OPEN — a node's status moved and its description still described the old world. Should a status setter say so, and is one sentence in a reply enough?
properties.rationale:
Recorded rather than built because A, B and C are three different sizes and the choice is not obvious, and because option C carries a measured failure from the person proposing it — which is the most useful thing in the report and would be lost if this were filed as "add a detector".

Note also what this is NOT: it is not the unchecked-prose class this session has been tracking in reflow2's own text. That class is reflow2 describing ITSELF wrongly. This is a USER's prose drifting from a USER's state, in their design — the same disease in the other direction, which is some evidence the problem is the medium rather than any one author's carelessness.
